Sections, stable-first: (1) THE MAP — the richest areas at steering grain; (2) AREA INDEX — every other area, named, one line each; (3) ACTIVE SURFACE — recent + load-bearing witnesses; (4) FOCUS — material loaded for your focus, LAST. The map and index never vary with your focus; your per-call material is at the end.

^-marked entries are compressed stubs carrying child addresses. Their narration and any surfaced witness quotes are verbatim-accurate — quote them as-is — but a stub carries no provenance (source, date, supersession). Expand (aswritten_expand with the IRIs you need) before any claim that turns on WHEN or by WHOM something was said, or whether it is still the current framing. Witness-depth sections below already carry full provenance.

Deciding where to go: each mapped area's narration tells you the SPAN of what lives under it; the area index names everything else. Expand a subtree when its narration (or name) shows your subject plausibly lives there — you'll get the trajectory, the variants, and the verbatim witness. But be strict about absence: if neither the map's narrations nor the index's names substantively cover your subject, it is NOT in this perspective — say so rather than expanding a loose thematic match (a word-overlap is not coverage). Decide from the map; expand to ground.

positions.name: OwnedVsRentedIntelligenceValue
positions.frame: Where does retained value reside when intelligence is owned rather than rented — in the substrate or in the perspective?
positions.why: Both expressions perform the same directional move across several dimensional reads: the value pass's OwnershipAsValueAxis mint ties them together as appeals to possession and self-origination as the good that separates keeper from renter; the register pass's AphoristicTechnicalMaxim mint marks both as the same jargon-free, matched-opposition crystallization of a technical distinction; the relational pass reads both as market-pricing framings (commodity/asset, owned/rented) allocating worth proportionally. There is a conviction-level tension worth holding rather than resolving: src-2 lands as a 'claim' — a firm assertion still argued for — while src-3 lands as a 'principle', constitutive bedrock the document itself (via src-4) frames as a restated thesis. The frame reads both together as one directional stance on where value sits in owned versus rented intelligence, without collapsing the difference in how settled each half is.

placements.why: The envelope's substantive content (src-2, src-3) is a positioning thesis about where value resides — owned versus rented intelligence, substrate as commodity versus perspective as retained asset. Existing strata is empty for this repo, and none of the canonical organizational-strategy categories (Opportunity/Strategy/Product/Architecture/Organization/Proof/Templates/Calibration) have been instantiated yet. This is positioning/value-proposition content, which is Strategy-grain, not Product or Architecture grain. Minting standalone since no parent strata exists or is needed — a strata mint does not require its ancestors to pre-exist.
placements.title: Positioning claims about where value is retained, not merely what capability exists
placements.frame: Does this content stake a claim about where the organization locates retained value or competitive standing, as distinct from product mechanics or architecture?

placements.title: Value in intelligence shifts from commodity substrate to owned perspective
placements.frame: Does this expression locate the retained, keepable value of intelligence in the owned perspective rather than in the fungible substrate or access layer beneath it?
placements.why: src-2 and src-3 perform one directional thematic move — 'Owned intelligence is not the same as rented intelligence' and 'The substrate is a commodity; the perspective is the asset you keep' — both stating, in matched aphoristic opposition, that ownership of perspective (not access to substrate) is where value is retained. This is narrative-grain per the grain test: it names a subject ('where value sits in owned vs rented intelligence') that future envelopes about positioning would keep feeding, not a one-time fact. The perspective's map and area index returned no coverage for this focus (confirmed by pass-2's resolution and pass-4's position framing), and both existing strata and existing graph structure are empty, so nothing existing can be reused — this is a genuine mint. The position pass already grouped these two segments as OwnedVsRentedIntelligenceValue, and the value-dimension's OwnershipAsValueAxis mint and register-dimension's AphoristicTechnicalMaxim mint both independently converge on this same content axis, reinforcing that it is a real, repeatable theme rather than a one-off phrasing.
